title: Inheritance
relevance: Inheritance, overriding, super(), and MRO are core OOP checks in SDE interviews and Python OAs.

phases.goal: Establish what inheritance is and how single inheritance reuses parent behavior.

must_hit.point: Inheritance lets a child/subclass derive properties and behaviors from a parent/base class.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Defines child deriving from parent, or subclass/base terminology.

must_hit.point: Inheritance promotes code reuse: a subclass inherits logic for free and can add or override behavior.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions reuse without rewriting shared logic, plus extending or overriding.

must_hit.point: In single inheritance, a child inherits from exactly one parent, passed as an argument in the class definition.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States one parent and shows class Child(Parent) form.

probes: What is inheritance, and how does single inheritance work in Python?

hints.1: Think about a new class getting behavior from an existing one.
hints.2: Contrast rewriting shared logic versus inheriting it, then adding or overriding.
hints.3: Child derives from one parent via class Dog(Animal); reuse plus override/add.

phases.goal: Cover overriding, super(), multiple inheritance, and how MRO/C3 resolves conflicts.

must_hit.point: Overriding means a child changes how a parent's method works; a child's __init__ completely replaces the parent's unless super() is used.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names overriding and that child __init__ replaces parent init without super().

must_hit.point: super() returns a temporary superclass object so you can call parent methods (e.g. parent __init__).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes calling the parent's method via super(), often in __init__.

must_hit.point: Python allows a class to inherit from multiple parents at once.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions multiple base classes in one class definition.

must_hit.point: MRO is the strict search order for methods/attributes; Python uses C3 Linearization so children precede parents and parent listing order is preserved.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names MRO and C3, plus child-before-parent and left-to-right parent order.

must_hit.point: In the diamond example D(B, C) with A at the top, d_obj.say() prints B; inspect order via __mro__ or .mro().
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says B wins for D(B, C) and mentions __mro__ or .mro().

probes: If you override __init__, how do you still run the parent's setup? What happens when two parents define the same method?

hints.1: Overriding replaces behavior; multiple parents need a search order.
hints.2: Use super() for parent __init__; MRO/C3 orders the diamond.
hints.3: Child __init__ replaces parent unless super().__init__(...); C3: children first, listed parent order; D(B,C) say prints B.

phases.goal: Contrast deep/wide inheritance with composition when multiple inheritance gets messy.

must_hit.point: Casual multiple inheritance is risky because MRO and state management (e.g. multiple super().__init__ calls) get very complex.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Flags MRO/state complexity with multiple inheritance and super init chains.

must_hit.point: Modern design favors composition (objects as attributes) over deep or wide inheritance trees.

probes: When would you avoid multiple inheritance in favor of another design?

hints.1: Think about overlapping parents and initialization.
hints.2: Compare inheriting many bases versus holding objects as attributes.
hints.3: Prefer composition over deep/wide trees when MRO and multi-super init get complex.

phases.goal: Apply overriding and recognize when multiple inheritance fails in practice.

must_hit.point: A subclass can override a parent method to change behavior (e.g. Penguin.fly printing Cannot fly instead of Flying).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives an override example where child behavior differs from parent.

must_hit.point: Multiple inheritance becomes unmaintainable when parents have complex overlapping state initializations; favor composition.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites overlapping state init as the failure mode and favors composition.

probes: Show how a subclass overrides a method, and when multiple inheritance breaks down.

hints.1: Start from a parent method and change it in the child.
hints.2: Override changes printed/behavior; failure is overlapping parent state init.
hints.3: Like Penguin overriding fly; overlapping multi-parent __init__ state → favor composition.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Inheritance reuses and extends parent behavior, but deep/wide or casual multiple inheritance makes MRO and multi-super().__init__ state management complex; modern design favors composition (objects as attributes) instead.
Multiple inheritance can mix behaviors from several parents, but same-named methods need MRO/C3 and diamond hierarchies get hard to trace; single inheritance avoids that conflict surface.

gotchas.trap: Assuming a child's __init__ still runs the parent's setup automatically.
gotchas.correction: The child's __init__ completely replaces the parent's; call super().__init__(...) when parent initialization is still needed.

gotchas.trap: Using multiple inheritance casually when parents share method names or complex init state.
gotchas.correction: MRO (C3) decides which method wins, and overlapping state initializations become a tangled mess—favor composition.

gotchas.trap: Thinking method conflicts in a diamond have no deterministic rule.
gotchas.correction: MRO via C3 Linearization gives a strict order: children before parents, and parent listing order preserved (e.g. D(B, C) → say prints B).
